title: Lead RRP pre-renovation information and recordkeeping practice questions
description: Free Lead RRP practice questions on pamphlet delivery and records under 40 CFR 745.84 and 745.86. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: A firm certifies in writing under 745.84(a)(2)(i) that it delivered the pamphlet to a dwelling but could not get an adult occupant's written acknowledgment. Which item must that certification include?

options.A: The occupant's date of birth
options.B: The reason for lack of acknowledgment, such as the occupant refusing to sign or no adult occupant being available
options.C: The owner's signature on the occupant's behalf
options.D: A photograph of the pamphlet at the door

questions.explanation: The certification "must include the address of the unit undergoing renovation, the date and method of delivery of the pamphlet, names of the persons delivering the pamphlet, reason for lack of acknowledgment (e.g., occupant refuses to sign, no adult occupant available), the signature of a representative of the firm performing the renovation, and the date of signature."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which renovations does 745.82(b) exempt from the 745.84 information distribution requirements?

options.A: Renovations in common areas of multi-unit target housing
options.B: Exterior renovations
options.C: Renovations in owner-occupied units
options.D: Emergency renovations

questions.explanation: "The information distribution requirements in § 745.84 do not apply to emergency renovations", which are activities "that were not planned but result from a sudden, unexpected event".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.82, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which copies does the 745.83 definition of "pamphlet" include?

options.A: Reproductions copied in full and without revision or deletion of material, except for adding or revising State or local sources of information
options.B: A one-page summary prepared by the firm
options.C: Any lead safety brochure the firm chooses to hand out
options.D: Excerpts of the pages that apply to the job

questions.explanation: The definition "includes reproductions of the pamphlet when copied in full and without revision or deletion of material from the pamphlet (except for the addition or revision of State or local sources of information)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.83, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.84(a)(2), when must the firm also give the pamphlet to an adult occupant of a dwelling unit?

options.A: Only when the occupant asks for it
options.B: Only when children under 6 live in the unit
options.C: When the owner does not occupy the dwelling unit
options.D: Only when the renovation is on the exterior

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(2) applies "if the owner does not occupy the dwelling unit": the firm must "provide an adult occupant of the unit with the pamphlet".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.84(a)(2)(i), what may the firm do if it delivered the pamphlet but could not get a written acknowledgment from an adult occupant?

options.A: Certify in writing that the pamphlet was delivered to the dwelling and that it was unsuccessful in obtaining a written acknowledgment
options.B: Ask the owner to sign on the occupant's behalf
options.C: Notify EPA and then begin work
options.D: Have one of its workers sign as a witness in place of the occupant

questions.explanation: The firm may "certify in writing that a pamphlet has been delivered to the dwelling and that the firm performing the renovation has been unsuccessful in obtaining a written acknowledgment from an adult occupant."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For a renovation in common areas of multi-unit target housing, what does 745.84(b)(3) require the firm to prepare, sign, and date?

options.A: A list of lead test results for every affected unit
options.B: A floor plan of the work area for each occupant
options.C: A waiver signed by each occupant
options.D: A statement describing the steps performed to notify all occupants of the intended renovation activities and to provide the pamphlet

questions.explanation: The firm must "Prepare, sign, and date a statement describing the steps performed to notify all occupants of the intended renovation activities and to provide the pamphlet."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Common areas of multi-unit target housing
questions.question: Under 745.84(b)(2)(i), what must the written notice to each affected unit describe for a common area renovation?

options.A: The names of the workers on the crew
options.B: The lead test results for each affected unit
options.C: The general nature and locations of the planned work, the expected starting and ending dates, and how to obtain the pamphlet and the records at no cost
options.D: The firm's insurance coverage

questions.explanation: "The notice shall describe the general nature and locations of the planned renovation activities; the expected starting and ending dates; and a statement of how the occupant can obtain the pamphlet and a copy of the records required by § 745.86(c) and (d), at no cost to the occupants".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Common areas of multi-unit target housing
questions.question: What is the alternative in 745.84(b)(2)(ii) to written notice for occupants of units affected by a common area renovation?

options.A: E-mailing the building manager
options.B: Posting informational signs while the renovation is ongoing where occupants of all affected units are likely to see them
options.C: Holding a tenant meeting before work starts
options.D: Leaving pamphlets in the lobby with no signs

questions.explanation: The firm may, "While the renovation is ongoing, post informational signs"; "These signs must be posted in areas where they are likely to be seen by the occupants of all of the affected units."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Common areas of multi-unit target housing
questions.question: Under 745.84(b)(4), what triggers further written notification to owners and occupants for a common area renovation?

options.A: A change in the scope, locations, or expected starting and ending dates after the initial notification, where the firm gave written initial notification to each affected unit
options.B: Any change in the crew members
options.C: The end of the renovation
options.D: An occupant's request for a second pamphlet

questions.explanation: "If the scope, locations, or expected starting and ending dates of the planned renovation activities change after the initial notification, and the firm provided written initial notification to each affected unit", the firm "must provide further written notification".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.84(c)(1)(ii), who must receive the pamphlet when the child-occupied facility is not the owner of the building?

options.A: Each child's teacher
options.B: The local health department
options.C: The State child care licensing office
options.D: An adult representative of the child-occupied facility

questions.explanation: "If the child-occupied facility is not the owner of the building, provide an adult representative of the child-occupied facility with the pamphlet".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which is one of the options in 745.84(c)(2) for giving parents and guardians the pamphlet and renovation information?

options.A: Giving the information to the facility director only
options.B: Mailing or hand-delivering the pamphlet and renovation information to each parent or guardian of a child using the facility
options.C: Publishing a notice in a local newspaper
options.D: Posting the information on the firm's website

questions.explanation: One option is to "Mail or hand-deliver the pamphlet and the renovation information to each parent or guardian of a child using the child-occupied facility."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.84(c)(2), besides the pamphlet, what must parents and guardians of children using a child-occupied facility be given before a renovation there?

options.A: Each child's blood lead test result
options.B: A copy of the firm's application for certification
options.C: Information describing the general nature and locations of the renovation and the anticipated completion date, and how they can review or obtain a copy of the records required by 745.86(c) and (d)
options.D: A daily schedule of each worker's hours

questions.explanation: The firm must provide them "with the pamphlet, information describing the general nature and locations of the renovation and the anticipated completion date, and information on how interested parents or guardians of children frequenting the child-occupied facility can review a copy of the records required by § 745.86(c) and (d) or obtain a copy from the renovation firm at no cost to the occupants".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.84(d)(2), what form may a written acknowledgment of receipt take?

options.A: A verbal confirmation noted by the crew
options.B: A notarized affidavit only
options.C: A form filed with EPA only
options.D: Either a separate sheet or part of any written contract or service agreement for the renovation

questions.explanation: The acknowledgment must "Be either a separate sheet or part of any written contract or service agreement for the renovation."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.84, Information distribution requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What must a certified renovator's test kit records include under 745.86(b)(1)(ii)?

options.A: The manufacturer and model of the kits used, a description of the components tested and their locations, and the result of each kit
options.B: The purchase price of the kits
options.C: The occupant's signature on each result
options.D: Photographs of each test swab

questions.explanation: The records must include "an identification of the manufacturer and model of any test kits used, a description of the components that were tested including their locations, and the result of each test kit used."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 745.86(a) say about how the firm's 3-year record retention requirement relates to longer retention obligations under other provisions?

options.A: It replaces any longer State or Tribal retention period
options.B: It does not supersede longer obligations under other provisions for retaining the same documentation, including applicable State or Tribal laws or regulations
options.C: It applies only to records that EPA has already requested
options.D: It ends early if the firm's certification expires

questions.explanation: "This 3-year retention requirement does not supersede longer obligations required by other provisions for retaining the same documentation, including any applicable State or Tribal laws or regulations."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.86(b)(6), what must a firm document if it could not comply with all requirements of the rule because of an emergency as defined in 745.82?

options.A: The occupant's written consent to skip the steps
options.B: EPA's prior approval of the change
options.C: The nature of the emergency and the provisions of the rule that were not followed
options.D: Nothing, because emergency renovations are exempt from recordkeeping

questions.explanation: "the firm must document the nature of the emergency and the provisions of the rule that were not followed." Section 745.82(b) also states emergency renovations are not exempt from "the recordkeeping requirements of § 745.86(b)(6) and (b)(7)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For a renovation within a residential dwelling, to whom must the firm provide compliance information under 745.86(c)(1)?

options.A: The owner of the building and, if different, an adult occupant of the residential dwelling
options.B: EPA only
options.C: An adult occupant only, and never the owner of the building
options.D: The local building department

questions.explanation: The firm must provide it to "The owner of the building; and, if different," "An adult occupant of the residential dwelling, if the renovation took place within a residential dwelling".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.86(c)(2), how must firms share compliance information after renovating common areas of multi-unit target housing?

options.A: Mail it to the local housing authority
options.B: Post the information, or instructions on how to obtain a copy, where it is likely to be seen by the occupants of all affected units
options.C: Send it to EPA within 30 days
options.D: Give it to the owner only

questions.explanation: Firms "must post the information required by this subpart or instructions on how interested occupants can obtain a copy of this information", "in areas where it is likely to be seen by the occupants of all of the affected units."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.86(d), what triggers the firm's duty to provide a copy of a dust sampling report to the owner and occupant?

options.A: An occupant's written request
options.B: Any use of an EPA-recognized test kit
options.C: Any renovation in a child-occupied facility
options.D: Dust clearance sampling performed in lieu of cleaning verification as permitted by 745.85(c)

questions.explanation: "If dust clearance sampling is performed in lieu of cleaning verification as permitted by § 745.85(c), the renovation firm must provide" "a copy of the dust sampling report".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.86(c)(3), what form may the firm use to provide the required compliance information?

options.A: Only an EPA-issued certificate
options.B: Only a copy of the final invoice
options.C: The "Sample Renovation Recordkeeping Checklist" or a similar form containing the test kit information and the training and work practice compliance information
options.D: Only a letter signed by the owner

questions.explanation: The information "may be provided by completing the sample form titled “Sample Renovation Recordkeeping Checklist” or a similar form containing the test kit information required by § 745.86(b)(1)(ii) and the training and work practice compliance information required by § 745.86(b)(6)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.86, Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)
